lessonRef.subject: financial-literacy
lessonRef.title: Correction and reflection: reaching a goal and choosing next
lessonRef.focus: reaching a goal and choosing next

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy Financial Literacy elementary sequence — Grade 3
Manuel Academy Financial Literacy G3 Unit 4 — saving and goals
objective: Learners work out what is left after a savings goal is reached and spent, then measure the distance to a fresh goal and the weeks needed to close it.
scenario: Marcus is an imaginary third grader who has reached his pretend $8.00 goal and bought an invented telescope kit priced at $6.50. He now wants an invented $5.00 star map and can save $1.00 of play money a week.
safetyNotes: Every amount, person, business, and account in this task is invented for practice. Nothing here refers to a real household.
Never write a real bank account, card, PIN, password, Social Security, or tax number on this sheet; the task never asks for one.
This is education, not individualized financial advice. Real money decisions belong to a trusted adult.

tasks.directions: Marcus spends $6.50 of his $8.00 on the telescope kit.

prompts.text: How much does Marcus have left after the telescope kit?

tasks.directions: Marcus points what is left toward the new $5.00 star map, and checks how far away that goal is before saving another week.

prompts.text: How much more does Marcus need for the $5.00 star map?
Right now, how does what Marcus has compare with the star map?

tasks.directions: Marcus saves $1.00 a week for the next four weeks on top of what he has.

prompts.text: How much does Marcus have after those four weeks?
How much is that past the $5.00 star map?

tasks.directions: Marcus did not start his second goal from zero.

prompts.text: Reaching one goal left Marcus with $1.50. How did that change the start of his next goal?

remediation: If a learner restarts at zero, keep the leftover coins physically on the table when the telescope card is removed, so the next goal visibly begins with money already present.
extension: Ask the learner what Marcus should do with the $0.50 he ends up over the goal, and to give a reason for the choice.
